Alex.confusing: Nothing major; the bonus scoring wasn't obvious at first, and my round 1 egg draws before the first night (3 to 5 cards) caught me briefly off guard.
Alex.fun: The round 2 Eagle read: seeing the visitor list for Blair, then catching Drew in a lie about who spoke first, and throwing 10 cards to bank 65 points.
Alex.change: Give Meowfia more ways to find each other or to hide a reveal; as the Mouser my round 1 position was fragile once the Kookaburra exposed me.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed Pigeon and winked Finley, which made me look guiltier. Instead I might have deflected onto Drew more subtly and not winked so early, though it did cost Finley's vote.

Blair.confusing: How the final score counts the pile and the nest. Alex's 10-card throw showed that nest size and throw volume matter a lot, and that wasn't obvious up front.
Blair.fun: Catching Drew in round 2 by checking his nest size against his claimed egg count. The table then piled onto him.
Blair.change: Give players a bit more information about how the bonus and the egg-gain mechanics play out. As it was, one player drawing 5 eggs let them overtake everyone.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw 3 cards at Drew when the vote was already lopsided. I should have thrown just 1 or 2 and kept more cards, or tried to get more eggs earlier. Alex finished with 69 to my 49 because of a 10-card throw and a bond bonus, and I never tried to beat that.

Casey.confusing: How the bonus and the throw economy interact: Alex threw 10 cards and banked 65 points, and I didn't see how much hand size and the Wattle bond decided the outcome.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when my Owl report showing a Hawk visited Drew exposed his lie and the table united to eggsecute him.
Casey.change: Show the hand-size changes more clearly, or cap how many eggs one player can gain from a night's visits, since Alex's big nest made him run away with the game.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw only 2 cards, and a Farm win was nearly certain. I should have thrown more, or bonded with someone. I also never tried the handshake, and I finished tied for second, so I lost.

Drew.confusing: Nest sizes being public made egg-count lies easy to catch, and it wasn't obvious how much my own draw count would give me away.
Drew.fun: Offering Alex the handshake and having it accepted. It was a gamble, and it paid +3 even though we lost.
Drew.change: I'd make Meowfia less of a sure loss. As the Sphinx I only learned the Farm roles, with no way to find my teammate, so I had little to work with.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I claimed "no eggs" and said I spoke first, and both were checkably false. I should have said I gained eggs, or claimed a role whose counts fit my nest, and I shouldn't have copied Casey's Kookaburra claim. In round 1 I should also not have offered a bond at the same moment I was under suspicion.

Ellis.confusing: How Alex's nest jumped to 11 and how the 5-egg cap and nest sizes interact with claims; also that throwing a whole nest scores so much more than keeping cards.
Ellis.fun: Catching Drew in round 2 through the nest-size and who-spoke-first contradictions, and the table converging on the right target.
Ellis.change: Make the Tit's guess less of a blind shot, for example by hinting at which roles are in play, so the role feels less useless.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I threw only 3 of my 4 cards, but I'd have banked more by also throwing my last one given the near-certain consensus. I also never used the handshake bond for +3 with a trusted Farm player.

Finley.confusing: How nest sizes carried over between rounds and how bonus points and the Golden Wattle bond interacted with the final scores.
Finley.fun: Working out in round 2 that Drew was lying, using the Owl visitor list and the nest-size math.
Finley.change: Make the Wink less punishing, or let a dead player still say something. Getting killed right after exposing the Mouser took me out of the round's talking.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I announced the Mouser result loudly, which got me winked. I should have kept it quiet or shared it in a less targeted way. I also should have thrown more of my cards at the confirmed Meowfia in round 2, or bonded with a trusted Farm player to gain points, since I finished 5th.

review.title: The Eagle's Big Nest
review.headline: The outed Mouser lost round one, then won the game with one 65-point throw.
review.summary: Drew was Meowfia in both rounds, and both times the table caught him easily by cross-checking info roles. In round 1 Alex was outed as the Mouser. He winked Finley, which only confirmed it, but the Farm still voted out his partner Drew. In round 2 Alex was a Farm Eagle. Four players visited his target, so he grew to 11 cards and threw 10 of them at the obvious Sphinx. That one throw took him from last place to a 20-point win.

rounds.recap: Blair's Hawk egg on Drew and Casey's Owl report put Drew under suspicion, and Finley's Kookaburra caught Alex as the Mouser. Alex winked Finley and Drew publicly shook hands with Alex, which made both look worse. The Farm piled 8 votes on Drew, and Meowfia lost.

Finley's Owl saw a Sphinx among Blair's visitors, and both Casey and Drew claimed Kookaburra. Drew then falsely said he had spoken first, and Blair accused him with wrong nest math. Five players threw at Drew, a lone Meowfia, and he was eggsecuted in beat 2.

highlights.text: Casey caught Alex's Pigeon claim on the spot: Alex said he visited Casey as a Pigeon, but Casey got no egg.
Finley named Alex as the Mouser and collapsed one beat later, which was close to a confession.
Drew offered Alex a public handshake to bank +3 each in a round they expected to lose, and Ellis read the bond as proof.
Alex went from last place to first by throwing 10 cards for 65 points.

confusions.what: His private note said he would name Hawk with the Sphinx, but he named Owl. That only found Casey, which was useless to him.
Thought Pigeon was the likeliest role to guess. With 4 Farm players and 8 Farm animals in the pool, nobody is a Pigeon unless Farm animals run out.
Said Alex gained 5 eggs. Alex gained 4: he had 5 cards, drew 2 at setup and got 4 at night. Casey and Drew repeated the 5.
Claimed Drew should have 5 cards, so his 6 meant hidden eggs. Drew had 4 after round 1, drew 2 at setup and gained none, so 6 was correct. The 2-card setup draw was forgotten.
Repeated Blair's wrong nest math as evidence against Drew.
As Sphinx he knew Kookaburra was a Farm role in play, yet he claimed it, which guaranteed a counterclaim. A role that was not in play would have been safe.

worked: Owl plus Hawk cross-check: Casey's Owl report confirmed Blair's Hawk visit to Drew in round 1. That made a clean, fair puzzle from two independent sources.
The Owl lists the animals that visited, including cats: Finley seeing 'Sphinx' in round 2 proved one of the claimants was lying and set up a real counterclaim.
Visible nest sizes: Casey used them to disprove Alex's Pigeon claim in round 1. Players actively checked counts, even when they got the math wrong.
Golden Wattle created a real decision for the losing side: Drew's bond with Alex earned +3 each but publicly tied him to the exposed Mouser.
problems: Nest size snowballs into score. Nests carry over, every card can be thrown at full value, and an Eagle at a crowded target gains up to 5 eggs. Alex won the game on one lucky visit and lost round 1 without consequence. Fix: cap cards thrown per vote (for example 5), or score Eagle eggs at 1 each.

Info roles crush Meowfia. Kookaburra hard-confirms a cat, and the Owl names Sphinx outright. Meowfia lost both rounds, and no vote was close. Fix: have the Owl report only the number of visitors, or let cats register as a Farm animal to Owl and Kookaburra.

The Mouser's Wink confirms the Mouser. Killing the player who just named you is the only sensible use, and dead players still score their throws, so Finley lost nothing but her 3 votes. Fix: let the Wink also void the victim's throw for scoring, or let the Mouser wink only before the day starts.

Golden Wattle handshakes are public and immediate, so offering one gives away your read. Only the Meowfia used it, and it rewarded a losing team with +3 each. Fix: make bonds secret until round end, or pay the Meowfia bonus only if their side wins.

The day ends too fast and alignment repeats. Both days ended at beat 2 on unanimous CAWs, Drew was Meowfia twice, and his score of 9 left him nothing to play for. Also, Casey's line appeared after the day had ended, which looks like an app ordering bug. Fix: require a minimum number of beats before CAW counts, and avoid giving the same player Meowfia in back-to-back rounds.
